clarifyingQuestions: Is dedupe scoped per channel or global?
Should repeated dedupe keys return a retry time or a permanent duplicate signal?
Is the window rolling or fixed?
followUps: Move counters to Redis with atomic updates.
followUpGuide: For hierarchy, check most-specific policy first but account against every required dimension atomically.
For weights, store remaining capacity and deduct each notification's cost.

For Redis, use a per-channel sorted set with dedupe keys as members and accepted timestamps as scores. In one atomic script or function, remove scores <= now - window, check the duplicate, check capacity, and insert only if allowed. A whole-key TTL may reclaim idle channels but cannot expire individual rolling-window members.
complexityAnalysis: - Each call filters and scans one channel. Time: O(k), where k is that channel's retained records (at most limit). Space: O(k) temporary; O(C + E) total for C remembered channels and E retained events. Idle channels can retain stale records until accessed.
- With a deque plus a key-to-timestamp map per channel, duplicate lookup is average O(1) and expiry is amortized O(1) per accepted event. A deque alone still needs an O(k) duplicate scan.
- Distributed follow-up moves expiry, duplicate lookup, capacity checks, and insertion into one atomic operation.
solutionGuide: Keep `(timestamp, dedupe_key)` records per channel. Remove expired records before dedupe or capacity checks.
